thread:
maria_support: Customer complaint TL;DR — web app users in EU seeing 500-800ms extra p99. Traced to requests routed to us-east instead of eu-central. Suspect header from browser fetch. Repro steps below.

sam_infra: can you paste a minimal repro curl and a request-id from the logs? also, any proxy in front of the browser?

maria_support: repro (from user's browser):
```js
fetch('https://api.redwood.test/v1/generate', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: {
    'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    'X-Client-Region': '' // sometimes blank in this app flow
  },
  body: '{}'
})
```
curl repro we ran (server-side):
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.test/v1/generate -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "X-Client-Region: " -d '{}'
```
example request-id: req_20260317_eu_user_01 (seen in access logs) routed to node us-east-5

ben_edge: saw the logs, thanks. Router received header as a single header with empty value. Current router logic: split header on comma, take first token, if token falsy -> treat as unspecified -> route to default edge (us by config). So an empty first token causes fallback.

li_ops: a few extra notes: Chrome fetch with some CORS/preflight combos can end up sending an empty header if the app sets header value from a missing form field. Also some intermediate proxies will concat duplicate headers into a CSV and our parser doesn't trim empty tokens.

sam_infra: short-term mitigation ideas: 1) tell customer to not send header when unknown (omit instead of empty string) 2) enforce trimming/skip-empty on router parsing (we can patch quickly) 3) for browser SDK, normalise region value or prefer ?region=eu param. Which do we want to push?

maria_support: customer wants a fix now — users in EU are hitting p99 +500ms. They can ship a quick client change but need a temporary server-side safeguard.

li_ops: I'm going to push a hotfix to router to ignore empty/whitespace tokens when parsing X-Client-Region. Patch will treat header value ",eu" the same as "eu" and "" as absent. Low risk. I'll also add logging to count occurrences. Deploy ETA ~ 45m.

incident_bot: Incident created: INC-20260317-237 — misroute due to empty region header. Pager notify to edge-oncall.

tara_billing: flagging billing/metrics: routing to different region could change token cost (eg cross-region egress) and will affect per-route metrics. Add a note to the incident if any customers report unexpected charges.

ben_edge: root cause summary for incident: client apps sometimes set X-Client-Region header to an empty string (or frontends concatenate with leading comma). Router parsing took first CSV token without trimming — empty token => treated as unspecified => default routing (us). Fix: trim and skip empties; also prefer last non-empty token to support case where proxies append.

sam_infra: followups: 1) patch merged & rolling out to canary (edge-canary) 2) add unit tests for headers like: "", ",eu", " , us", "eu,us" 3) update SDK docs recommending omitting header when unknown and prefer query param as explicit override.

maria_support: forwarding update to customer. Thanks folks. :pray:

li_ops: will post deployment completion and counts of affected requests in ~45m.

maria_support: also note: customer reported one request-id that had mixed-case header 'X-client-region: ,EU' — our parsing should be case-insensitive. Added to test matrix.

ben_edge: good catch. will include case-normalisation.

incident_bot: INC-20260317-237 status: monitoring after rollback-safe deploy.

maria_support: marking this thread for customer follow-up once deploy is green.
